question: Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed pages 412 and 413, noted not translated. नेता (*netā*): the root णीञ् प्रापणे (*ṇīñ prāpaṇe*), the affix tṛc in the agent sense; na for the initial ṇa by णोनः (*ṇonaḥ*); the affix ktic by क्तिच्‌क्तौचसंज्ञायां (*kticktaucasaṃjñāyāṃ*) (Pā. 3-3-174); no guṇa because the affix is k-marked; genitive plural; the udātta on the case ending of the nāmin (long vowel stem) by नामन्यतरस्यां (*nāmanyatarasyāṃ*) (Pā. 6-1-177). दैवीनां (*daivīnāṃ*): on the word deva in the sense of relation, the affix añ by देवाद्यञञ् (*devādyañañ*); vṛddhi of the first syllable by तद्धितेष्वचामादेः (*taddhiteṣvacāmādeḥ*) (Pā. 7-2-117); in the feminine the affix ṅīp by टिड्ढाण् (*ṭiḍḍhāṇ*) (Pā. 4-1-15), which is anudātta, so that the preceding affix is udātta; genitive plural. ऋतुपाः (*ṛtupāḥ*): the root पा रक्षणे (*pā rakṣaṇe*); the affix vic by अन्येभ्योपिदृश्यंते (*anyebhyopidṛśyaṃte*) (Pā. 3-2-75); compound with the upapada by उपपदमतिज् (*upapadamatij*) (Pā. 2-2-19); since the upapada stands in a kāraka relation, the accent of the second member by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) (Pā. 6-2-139) (the Kannada text reads ಕೈಮತ್ತರಪದಪ್ರಕೃತಿಸ್ವರ, as supplied). ऋतावा (*ṛtāvā*): the affix vasip in the sense of possession by the Vedic rule छंदसीवनिपौ (*chaṃdasīvanipau*); lengthening of the preceding vowel in the Saṃhitā by अन्येषामपि दृश्यते (*anyeṣāmapi dṛśyate*) (Pā. 6-3-137); the affix is p-marked and so anudātta. वृत्रहा (*vṛtrahā*): the root हन हिंगत्योः (*hana hiṃgatyoḥ*) (printed so; the bhāṣya has ಹಿಂಸಾಗತ್ಯೋಃ); with vṛtra as upapada, the affix kvip by ब्रह्मभ्रूणवृत्रेषु क्विप् (*brahmabhrūṇavṛtreṣu kvip*) (Pā. 3-2-87); the accent of the second member of a compound; nominative singular. विश्ववेदाः (*viśvavedāḥ*): a bahuvrīhi; the accent on the last syllable of the first member by बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायां (*bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyāṃ*) (Pā. 6-106, as supplied). पर्षत् (*parṣat*): the root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*); liṭ-like Vedic leṭ, third person singular, tip; loss of the i by इतश्चलोपः (*itaścalopaḥ*) (Pā. 3-4-97); sip by सिब्बहुलं लेटि (*sibbahulaṃ leṭi*) (Pā. 3-1-34); the augment aṭ by लेटोडाटौ (*leṭoḍāṭau*) (Pā. 3-4-94); guṇa of the ṛ of the root by सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोः (*sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ*) (Pā. 7-3-84); r follows; no nighāta because the word stands at the beginning of a pāda; the augment being anudātta, the accent of the root remains. दुरिता (*duritā*): the root इण् गत् (*iṇ gat*) (printed so) with the affix t; the accent of the second member in the compound; in the neuter plural loss of śi by शेश्छंदसि बहुलं (*śeśchaṃdasi bahulaṃ*). गृणंतं (*gṛṇaṃtaṃ*): the root गृ शब्दे (*gṛ śabde*), kryādi class; the substitute śatṛ for laṭ; the vikaraṇa śnā by क्रादिभ्यः श्ना (*krādibhyaḥ śnā*) (Pā. 3-1-81); since śatṛ is ś-marked, loss of the ā of the vikaraṇa by श्नाभ्यस्तयोरातः (*śnābhyastayorātaḥ*) (Pā. 6-4-112); ṇatva of the n after ṛ; question: Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed page 444, noted not translated. अर्णं (*arṇaṃ*): the root ऋ गतौ (*ṛ gatau*); by उदके नुट्‌च (*udake nuṭca*) (U. Sū. 4-637) the affix asun, to which comes the augment नुडागम (*nuḍāgama*); because it is ṭ-marked (printed टित्तादुदरिंद (*ṭittādudariṃda*)) it comes as the first part. आर्यते-प्रार्थ्यते तत्पिपासुभिरिति अर्णः (*āryate-prārthyate tatpipāsubhiriti arṇaḥ*) ("that which is prayed for by the thirsty"); by Vedic usage the final sa is elided; since the affix is nit-marked, by इत्न्यत्यादिर्नित्यं (*itnyatyādirnityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-197) (printed so) the initial-udātta accent comes. अच्छ (*accha*): by निपातस्य च (*nipātasya ca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-136) lengthening in the Saṃhitā. जिगासि (*jigāsi*): the root गा स्तुत् (*gā stut*) (printed so), used only in the Veda; here, because of the particle ca, it is used in the sense of going; juhotyādi class; laṭ, second person singular, sip; doubling of the root on account of ślu (श्लु (*ślu*)); by बहुलं छेदसि (*bahulaṃ chedasi*) (printed so) the vowel i for the reduplicative; because it stands after an atiṅanta (printed अतिजंत (*atijaṃta*)) the nighāta accent comes. ऊचिषे (*ūciṣe*): the root ब्रूञ् व्यक्तायां वाचि (*brūñ vyaktāyāṃ vāci*); liṭ, second person singular; by थासः से (*thāsaḥ se*) the substitution se; when this affix, which has the ārdhadhātuka designation, follows, by ब्रुवोवचिः (*bruvovaciḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 2-4-53) (the opening bracket of the reference is missing in the print) the substitution vaci for the root; by असंयोगाल्लिट्‌कित् (*asaṃyogālliṭkit*) (Pā. Sū. 1-2-5) the affix is k-marked, and therefore by वजिस्वपियजा (*vajisvapiyajā*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-15) the va of the root becomes u by samprasāraṇa, with पूर्वरूप (*pūrvarūpa*) for the a; by लिट्यभ्यासस्योभयेषां (*liṭyabhyāsasyobhayeṣāṃ*) samprasāraṇa and पूर्वरूप (*pūrvarūpa*) also for the va of the reduplicative; by अर्धधातुकस्येड्वलादेः (*ardhadhātukasyeḍvalādeḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 7-2-35) the augment iḍ for the affix; by आदेशप्रत्यययोः (*ādeśapratyayayoḥ*) ṣatva for the sa; because it stands after an atiṅanta the nighāta accent comes. The grammar continues on page 445.

Grammar of Ṛk 3, continued, printed page 445. धिष्ण्याः (*dhiṣṇyāḥ*): the root उष प्लुष दाहे (*uṣa pluṣa dāhe*); धियः उष्णंतीति धिष्ण्याः (*dhiyaḥ uṣṇaṃtīti dhiṣṇyāḥ*); since it is laid down as nipāta by सानसि धर्णसि पर्णसि तंडुलांकुश चषालेल्वल पल्वल धिष्ण्यशल्याः (*sānasi dharṇasi parṇasi taṃḍulāṃkuśa caṣālelvala palvala dhiṣṇyaśalyāḥ*) (U. Sū. 4-547), the augment नुडागम (*nuḍāgama*), धात्वादिलोप (*dhātvādilopa*), the shortening of the upapada (धी (*dhī*)) and the like are accomplished without the operation of the sūtras; because it ends in an affix that is nit-marked (printed नित् (*nit*)) the initial-udātta accent comes. परस्तात् (*parastāt*): the affix अस्ताति (*astāti*) in the sense of the locative; by यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) elision of the preceding a; the initial-udātta accent of the affix. अवस्तात् (*avastāt*): the word अवर (*avara*); by दिक्‌छब्देभ्यः सप्तमीपंचमी (*dikchabdebhyaḥ saptamīpaṃcamī*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-27) the affix अस्ताति (*astāti*); when this follows, by विभाषावरस्य (*vibhāṣāvarasya*) (Pā. Sū. 5-3-41) the substitution अवादेश (*avādeśa*) for अवर (*avara*); the initial-udātta accent of the affix. उपतिष्ठंते (*upatiṣṭhaṃte*): the root ष्ठा गतिनिवृत्तौ (*ṣṭhā gatinivṛttau*); because of the connection with the preverb उप (*upa*), by अकर्वकाच्च (*akarvakācca*) (Pā. Sū. 1-3-26) (printed so) the ātmanepada comes; laṭ, third person plural form; by यद्वृत्तान्नित्यं (*yadvṛttānnityaṃ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-66), because of the connection with the word यच्छब्द (*yacchabda*), the nighāta accent does not come; by तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the लसार्वधातुक (*lasārvadhātuka*) becomes anudātta, so the accent of the root remains; by तिजुचोदात्तवति (*tijucodāttavati*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-71) the all-anudātta accent comes on the gati (उप (*upa*)).
The Saṃhitā has प्रावणेभिः (*prāvaṇebhiḥ*) where the Pada and the bhāṣya have प्रवणेभिः (*pravaṇebhiḥ*); noted, not corrected.

question: Grammar of Ṛk 4, printed page 447, noted not translated. पुरीष्यासः (*purīṣyāsaḥ*): the root पृ पालनपूरणयोः (*pṛ pālanapūraṇayoḥ*); the affix īṣan by शृ पृ भ्यांकित् (*śṛ pṛ bhyāṃkit*) (U. Sū. 4-467), and because it is k-marked there is no guṇa; the substitution u by उदोष्यः पूर्वस्य (*udoṣyaḥ pūrvasya*) (Pā.Sū. 7-1-10) (reference as printed), with r following. पुरीषं पृणातेः पूरयतीर्वा (*purīṣaṃ pṛṇāteḥ pūrayatīrvā*) (Siru. 2-22) is cited as Yāska's (abbreviation as printed). The affix ya by छंदसिच (*chaṃdasica*) (Pā. Sū. 5-1-67); the designation bha by यचिभं (*yacibhaṃ*); elision of the preceding a by यस्यॆतिच (*yasyètica*); the affix accent makes it final-udātta; after jas the augment asuk by आज्जसेरसुक् (*ājjaserasuk*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-50). प्रावणेभिः (*prāvaṇebhiḥ*): the root वन षण संभक्तौ (*vana ṣaṇa saṃbhaktau*); the affix gha in the sense of instrument by पुंसि संज्ञायां घःप्रायेण (*puṃsi saṃjñāyāṃ ghaḥprāyeṇa*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-118); the प्रवणानि (*pravaṇāni*) are the digging implements (हारॆ गुद्दलि मुंतादुवु (*hārè guddali muṃtāduvu*)); ṇatva of the root n by पुनिरंतः (*puniraṃtaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-4-5) (printed so); by वनंसमासे (*vanaṃsamāse*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-178) the final-udātta accent in the compound, or the kṛd-uttarapada accent; or, from the root पुज् गत् (*puj gat*), the affix yuṭ by चलनशब्दार्थादकर्मकाद्युट् (*calanaśabdārthādakarmakādyuṭ*) (Pā. Sū. 3-2-148). In the former alternative it must be said that the avagraha does not occur by Vedic usage. The grammar continues on page 448.

Grammar of Ṛk 1, printed page 454, noted not translated. निर्मथितः (*nirmathitaḥ*): the root मंथ विलोडने (*maṃtha viloḍane*); the affix kta in the passive; because it is kit, loss of the nasal of the root; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-49) the udātta accent for the gati. सुधितः (*sudhitaḥ*): the root डुधाण् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāṇ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*) (the bhāṣya has डुधाञ् (*ḍudhāñ*) in the other place); when kta comes in the passive, since it is irregularly formed by सुधितवसुधित नेमधित (*sudhitavasudhita nemadhita*) (Pā. Sū. 7-4-45), dhi is the substitute for the root; by गतिरनंतरः (*gatiranaṃtaraḥ*) the gati takes its own (prakṛti) accent. जूर्यत्सु (*jūryatsu*): the root जूरी घूरी हिंसावयोहान्योः (*jūrī ghūrī hiṃsāvayohānyoḥ*); by व्यत्ययोबहुलं (*vyatyayobahulaṃ*) śatṛ is the substitute for laṭ; by दिवादिभ्यः श्यन् (*divādibhyaḥ śyan*) (Pā. Sū. 3-1-69) the vikaraṇa śyan; because it follows what the print gives as अदुपदेश (*adupadeśa*), the lasārvadhātuka becomes anudātta; since śyan is nit, by इत्यादिर्नित्यं (*ityādirnityaṃ*) the initial-udātta accent comes; a form ending in the seventh case plural. अजरः (*ajaraḥ*): the root ज्यूष् वयोहानौ (*jyūṣ vayohānau*) (the bhāṣya has ज्ञ वयोहाना (*jña vayohānā*)); when the abstract sense is shown, by ऋदोरप् (*ṛdorap*) (Pā. Sū. 3-3-57) guṇa for the ṛ of the root, which comes with ra; न विद्यते जरा यस्य सः (*na vidyate jarā yasya saḥ*), by नञो जरमरमित्रमृताः (*naño jaramaramitramṛtāḥ*) (Pā. Sū 6-2-116, as printed) the accent udātta on the first syllable of the latter member. अत्र (*atra*): by ऋचि तुनुघ (*ṛci tunugha*) (Pā. Sū. 6-3-133) lengthening in the Saṃhitā (printed धीर्घ (*dhīrgha*)). दधे (*dadhe*): the root डुधाञ् धारणपोषणयोः (*ḍudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ*); liṭ in the present sense by Vedic usage; a form ending in the first person (printed प्रथमपुरुष (*prathamapuruṣa*)) singular; the tiṅanta-nighāta accent comes. जातवेदाः (*jātavedāḥ*): the root जनी प्रादुर्भावे (*janī prādurbhāve*); when the affix kta follows, by जनसनखनां सन्झलोः (*janasanakhanāṃ sanjhaloḥ*) (Pā.Sū. 6-4-42, as printed) ā as the final substitute of the root; जातं वेदः (*jātaṃ vedaḥ*) (ज्ञानं (*jñānaṃ*)) यस्य सः जातवेदाः (*yasya saḥ jātavedāḥ*); by बहुव्रीहौ प्रकृत्यापूर्वपदं (*bahuvrīhau prakṛtyāpūrvapadaṃ*) the pūrvapada-prakṛti accent; the former member becomes antodātta by the affix accent.

question: Grammar of Ṛk 3, printed page 508. क्रंदन् (*kraṃdan*): the root क्रदि आह्वाने रोदने च (*kradi āhvāne rodane ca*); for laṭ the substitute śatṛ; since it is marked idit, the augment num. By तास्यनुदात्तेत् (*tāsyanudāttet*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-186) the śatṛ becomes anudātta, so the accent of the root remains. युगेयुगे (*yugeyuge*): by नित्यवीप्सयोः (*nityavīpsayoḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-4) the doubling comes. By तस्यपरमाम्रेडितं (*tasyaparamāmreḍitaṃ*) the latter part gets the designation āmreḍita. By अनुदात्तंच (*anudāttaṃca*) (Pā. Sū. 8-1-3) it takes the sarvānudātta accent, so the accent of the nature of the former member remains. सुवीर्यम् (*suvīryam*): by वीर वीर्यौच (*vīra vīryauca*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-120) the ādyudātta accent of the latter member comes. स्वश्वं (*svaśvaṃ*): शोभनः अश्वः यस्य तत् (*śobhanaḥ aśvaḥ yasya tat*). Since the word aśva ends in the affix क्वन् (*kvan*) (printed so; as supplied) it is ādyudātta; by आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्‌छंदसि (*ādyudāttaṃ dvyacchaṃdasi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-2-119) the ādyudātta accent of the latter member comes in the compound. Here the letter ya has come in addition, as a Vedic usage. Or: अश्वेषु साधनः अश्वाः तत्रसाधुः (*aśveṣu sādhanaḥ aśvāḥ tatrasādhuḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 4-4-98) the affix yat in the sense "good at". By यस्येतिच (*yasyetica*) the preceding a is elided. By यतोनावः (*yatonāvaḥ*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-313) the ādyudātta accent comes, so in the bahuvrīhi the ādyudātta accent of the latter member comes as before.

question: Grammar of Ṛk 14, printed page 560. वृषो इति (*vṛṣo iti*): when the word is vṛṣa joined with उ (*u*), guṇa comes by आद्गुणः (*ādguṇaḥ*). By उञाः (*uñāḥ*) the उ (*u*) becomes uñ and has the designation pragṛhya (प्रगृहसंज्ञा (*pragṛhasaṃjñā*) in the supplied text); therefore, relying on the uñ in the ओ (*o*) (relying on the treatment of the single substitute as if it were the following or the preceding sound), the designation प्रगृह्यसंज्ञा (*pragṛhyasaṃjñā*) comes at the stage of the pada. Hence there is no scope for the avādeśa and other sandhi operations. देववाहनः (*devavāhanaḥ*): वह प्रापणे (*vaha prāpaṇe*) is the root. By हेतुमतिच (*hetumatica*) the affix ṇic. By अत उपधायाः (*ata upadhāyāḥ*) vṛddhi comes to the penultimate of the root (the supplied word is उपधानकारक्कॆ (*upadhānakārakkè*)). After the ṇyanta the affix lyu in the agent. By णेरनिटि (*ṇeraniṭi*) (Pā. Sū. 6-4-51) the ṇic is elided. By युवोरनाकौ (*yuvoranākau*) (Pā. Sū. 7-1-1) the यु (*yu*) that remains in the affix lyu receives the substitute ana. By लिति (*liti*) (Pā. Sū. 6-1-193) the udātta accent comes on the syllable before the affix. When it becomes a compound, by गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् (*gatikārakopapadāt kṛt*) the accent of the final member's own base comes.
